page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ads_v7 is an Eadsv7-family virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is provisioned with 1890 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU testing, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory performance is strong, with Passmark memory scores in the top 25%, while large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations remain average. For language model tasks, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds with small 135M models but exhibits weak performance when processing prompts for large 70B models.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core, the E32-16ads_v7 offers qualitative resource density suited for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of higher vCPU counts. The inclusion of 1890 GB of local storage provides a built-in storage buffer for data-heavy operations. This hardware profile is well-suited for memory-optimized databases, text processing, caching layers, and small-scale language model inference, though it presents a tradeoff in multi-core scaling for highly parallelized compute tasks.
